problems: The caption's key moment, the rope catching round the big toadstool, can't be seen: in the 50% and 75% frames the rope segments meet behind or under the cap, which hides the stem. You can't tell whether the rope wraps round the toadstool or just ends at it.

You can't count or follow 'ten of us on one rope'. From storyboard frame 3 onward the tied animals bunch into one knot left of the tree. Red segments run in every direction through that clump, so a viewer can't tell which animals are on the rope or follow it from one end to the other. Small pigs and birds inside the fence (25%, 50%) look untied, which muddles it further.

The rope passes straight through the fence with no contact. In the 50% and 75% frames the red segments cross the rails into the pen and the fence doesn't react. At 75% the blue creature sits in the fence line.
The rope also cuts through animal bodies in the central clump (25% and 50%: red rods crossing the white sheep-like animal and the yellow bird).
The rope looks like stiff, thick red pipes. The segments are perfectly straight even where the animals have slack, so it doesn't read as a rope under tension.

'The pig is still pulling' isn't shown. Over the last eight storyboard frames the pig on the right barely moves and its pose stays the same; nothing shows it straining or the rope tightening because of it.
In storyboard frames 1–2 the rope runs off the left edge over the beach and water to an animal you can barely see, then snaps in. The opening is unreadable at this distance.
The camera is too far away. The animals, the rope and the toadstool fill a small part of the frame, and the sea and the empty meadow take up most of it.
posts.critique: From this distance it's a tangle of red rods in a crowd. The two things the caption promises, the rope caught round the toadstool and the pig pulling, can't be seen, and the rope passes through the fence and the animals without touching them.
